subject: Onboarding request: LLM-X-20B quant variant + version pin for pilot
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Onboarding request: LLM-X-20B (q4_k_m) for pilot

Hi Hannah / team,

Thanks for taking a look. Acme AI is planning a small commercial pilot with our joint customer (Acme Retail) and we'd like Redwood to host the LLM-X-20B q4_k_m quantized variant for the pilot window (Nov 20 - Jan 20). Our asks:

- Compatibility check for the provided quantized variant (q4_k_m) on your serving runtime, including KV cache behavior and continuous batching implications.
- Option to pin traffic to a vendor-specified model version for the pilot (we can provide a signed hash).
- A short performance report (latency P50/P95 for 256/1024 tokens, memory usage) and any recommended runtime flags.

Attached: llmx20b-release-notes.pdf, sample-inference-config.yaml. Full artifacts are on S3: https://s3.vendor.ai/llm-x/20b/q4_k_m/release/ (read-only token will be shared).

We can make the vendor team available for a 30m sync if helpful. Please let us know requirements and rough timeline.

Thanks,
Laura Chen
Partnerships, Acme AI

Attachment stubs: llmx20b-release-notes.pdf (4.2MB, PDF), sample-inference-config.yaml (YAML)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-11-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding request: LLM-X-20B (q4_k_m) for pilot

Laura — thanks, and appreciate the S3 link. Looping in infra (Dev) and applied ML (Marcus) + serving (Dylan) to scope compat checks and a pinning plan. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) We need the model artifact checksum (SHA256) and a recommended canonical name you want us to pin to (vendor-provided).
2) Dev: can you confirm infra constraints (GPU memory, quant libs supported) and estimate smoke-test turnaround?
3) Marcus/Dylan: can you list the minimal eval prompt set you'd like us to run during the smoke tests?

Tentative timeline: 3 business days for smoke compatibility tests once artifacts are accessible; full perf report within 7 business days. If results are clean, we'll prepare a pinned model config for the pilot.

If vendor can do a quick walkthrough Monday (11/3), that could shave time. Laura — are you available?

Hannah Schmitt
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-11-03T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding request: LLM-X-20B (q4_k_m) for pilot — infra plan

Thanks Hannah / Laura. I reviewed the release notes and the S3 bundle. Early notes and ask-list: 

- Supported quant format: q4_k_m (vendor-provided). We already have a prototype loader for q4_k_m but need to validate kernel pathing (cuBLAS vs custom CUDA kernel).
- Memory: expect ~70-90GB GPU RAM for 2048-token context in our current packing. Ensure we test both 256 and 1024 token cases.
- KV-cache: vendor uses a slightly different layout; we will run a KV-cache integrity test to ensure no corruption across batching.

Compatibility/validation checklist (smoke):
- Verify SHA256 of artifacts against vendor-supplied checksum.
- Load model into staging runtime and run single-token and streaming inference.
- Run KV-cache roundtrip test with 3 concurrent sessions.
- Latency sample: P50/P95 at 256/1024 tokens with our default batching.
- Perf: capture peak GPU memory and host CPU usage.

Estimated timeline: 3 business days for the smoke checklist once we have read access + checksum. If we hit kernel mismatches, plan + estimate will change (might need 1–2 weeks for kernel integration).

Attachments: compat-check-template.json (small checklist), perf-sample-log.txt

Action items for vendor/PM:
- Provide signed SHA256 and canonical pin name (example: llm-x-20b-q4-v20251101).
- Grant read access to S3 and share sample prompt set (minimal 50 prompts).

I'll start the staging run as soon as we have the checksum and access.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Infrastructure Engineering, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Date: 2025-11-04T11:33:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding request: LLM-X-20B (q4_k_m) for pilot — eval notes

Quick notes from applied ML:

- Before we pin, we need a small sanity eval: toxicity, instruction-following on 100 prompts, and a throughput-quality tradeoff check (temperature and top-p settings). I can run the eval once Dev confirms staging image is up.
- Suggest pin naming convention: vendor canonical name + date + quant tag. Example recommendation: llm-x-20b-20251101-q4_k_m. Pin to that for the pilot, with an automated fallback to a 13B open model (llama2-13b-202502) for high-latency incidents.
- Watchouts: quantized variants sometimes degrade rare-token handling — add a small prompt set targeting rare entity completion to the smoke tests.

If infra can provide perf numbers (P50/P95) and the SHA by EOD, I can run the eval and give a go/no-go within 24–36 hours.

Marcus Lin
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
